h1: Beverage training for global drinks company teams
title: Training for global drinks teams | Craft Beer School
desc: How we train drinks company teams anywhere: Beverage 101, operations, raw materials, sensory sessions and data, live online or on site by arrangement.
teaser: Your analysts and planners handle beer, whisky and wine data every day. Few have seen the product made.
standfirst: We run beverage training for teams in drinks companies and their shared service centres. Programmes are built around your own portfolio and run live online or on site by arrangement.
sections: The gap in many drinks teams

A forecast analyst, a procurement buyer or a finance partner in a drinks company often works on beer, whisky or wine for years without seeing a brewery, still or winery. They know the numbers and not the product. That makes some decisions harder than they should be: why a batch cannot be rushed, why a stock plan needs lead time, why a quality hold changes a forecast.

Training closes that gap. It does not turn people into brewers. It gives them enough product knowledge to ask better questions and to read their own data with more confidence.

The same is true of people who joined from other industries. Many of the best analysts in a drinks company came from banking, retail or technology. Product training lets them contribute with the context that long-serving colleagues already have.

Beverage 101. How beer, whisky and wine are made, in plain language, with the vocabulary teams meet in meetings.

Brewing and distilling operations. The plant, the process and the constraints: batch sizes, tank time, maturation, packaging lines.

Raw materials and supply chain. Barley, hops, grapes, water, yeast, glass and cans: what drives their price and availability.

Guided sensory sessions. A structured way of tasting and describing drinks, responsibly and by choice.

Data and AI in beverages. What good data looks like in a plant and where AI helps.

Route to market and regulation. How drinks reach consumers, at process level. Rules differ by country and change, so teams check current ones with their own compliance people.

Modules can be taken one at a time or combined. A planning team may want operations and supply chain. A finance team may start with Beverage 101 and data. A group of new joiners may take all of them over several weeks.

We do not teach from a generic slide deck. We ask which brands, styles and markets the team supports and use them. A team that works on lagers hears about lager fermentation. A team on single malt hears about cask maturation. Examples come from the products on their screens.

We keep product claims to well-established facts and name no company's plant or numbers. When your team wants to discuss internal figures, they do that with their own colleagues.
Live online anywhere, or on site

Programmes run live online for teams in any time zone, with sessions timed to local working hours. They can also be delivered on site by arrangement. Group size is agreed with the team lead so that questions can be asked. Recordings and notes are available for people who miss a session.

Tasting is optional and always within company policy. Non-drinkers are welcome and can take part with non-alcoholic options or as note-takers. Samples are small. Spit cups and water are provided and nobody is encouraged to drink more. In places where alcohol is restricted, we run the sessions with non-alcoholic products or without tasting.

Sessions are short enough to fit around work. We would rather run six one-hour sessions that people attend than one long day that nobody can follow.

After training, people tend to ask different questions of their data. They notice why a yield figure moves, why a seasonal peak needs earlier planning and why quality holds happen. Our piece on explaining brewery KPIs shows what this looks like. For a lighter start, see beer basics for shared service teams.

The first sign usually shows in meetings, not in a test. Questions get sharper. Instead of asking why a number moved, people ask which step moved it. That is the kind of thinking a data team needs in a production business.

Tell us who the team is, what they work on and what you want them to be able to do. We propose modules and a schedule. The same approach works for sales and marketing groups: see sensory training for sales teams.

There is no fixed fee list. Cost depends on team size, number of modules and format, so we quote after we know what you need.

We can start with a single pilot session for one team and extend it if it helps. That is often easier than committing a whole organisation at once.

Does the team need to drink alcohol?
No. Tastings are optional and within company policy, with non-alcoholic options and spit cups for anyone who prefers.
No. We build it around the portfolio, markets and roles of your team.

Yes. Modules cover beer, whisky and wine.
